title: uml-mcp: letting an AI draw the diagram

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You're chatting with an AI assistant and you say, draw me a sequence diagram of a user logging in through an API gateway. A moment later, the diagram appears in the chat.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How does it pull that off?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's uml-mcp, a Model Context Protocol server. The assistant writes the diagram source in PlantUML, Mermaid, D2, Graphviz and more, calls one of the server's tools, and gets back an image, a link to the rendered file and an editable playground link.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mostly Kroki. The source is compressed, put into a URL, and rendered there. If Kroki fails, the server can fall back to other renderers, and results are cached so repeat calls are quick.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What tools does the assistant get?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Five. Render one diagram, render one as an inline image, validate the source before rendering so the assistant can fix mistakes, list the diagram types, and render a batch in one call. The README counts 46 diagram types.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Does the user get more than a picture?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In clients that support MCP Apps, the diagram opens in a viewer inside the chat. You can zoom, edit the source, change the theme and export to SVG, PNG or PDF.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Use the hosted endpoint on Vercel, or install it from PyPI, or self-host with Docker or Helm. There are ready configurations for Cursor, VS Code and Claude Desktop.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So diagrams become part of the conversation.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's it. The full write-up has the step-by-step pipeline and the demo recording.
